title: introduce-init-orchestrator-dsl-and-airgap-image-verification
author: Anya Velasquez
release_notes: Adds an init orchestrator DSL for sequencing Helm hook Jobs and a preflight image verification step for air-gapped/private installs. Backoff and concurrency are configurable; includes values.schema updates and example airgap values file.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a small domain-specific orchestrator DSL inside the Helm templates to sequence tenant-scoped init Jobs, plus an optional preflight image verification job that validates images against a provided manifest or mirror. Motivation: private/on-prem installs in air-gapped environments require deterministic init sequencing and a way to verify that required container images are present in an offline mirror. The current hook model requires manual orchestration; this change centralizes policy and makes init phases declarative and auditable.

Checklist:
- [x] Add values.schema for new keys (initOrchestrator, airgapVerification)
- [x] Implement templates: _helpers.tpl, init-orchestrator-job.yaml, preflight-image-check.yaml, annotations and RBAC snippets
- [x] Add example values: tests/values-airgap.yaml and examples/airgap/README.md
- [x] Unit Helm template tests for sequencing and conditional rendering
- [x] Document runtime behavior in docs/private-installer.md

What changed (high level):
- charts/redwood-private-installer/templates/init-orchestrator-job.yaml: New templated Job that is rendered when .Values.initOrchestrator.enabled is true. The template accepts a small DSL: waves -> stages -> tasks. Waves are serialized with an ordinal and respect tenant-scoped concurrency and leader-election annotations. The Job uses a small init controller image (configurable) that interprets the DSL and executes defined sub-jobs via Kubernetes Job API.
- charts/redwood-private-installer/values.schema.json: Added schema for initOrchestrator and airgapVerification sections, with validation for required fields in airgap mode (manifestChecksum or mirrorRegistry).
- charts/redwood-private-installer/templates/_helpers.tpl: New helper functions to render DSL JSON blobs and stable names for orchestrated Jobs and to emit safe annotations for audit logs.
- charts/redwood-private-installer/templates/preflight-image-check.yaml: Optional preflight Job that validates the presence and digest of images against a provided image-manifest ConfigMap or offline registry credentials. Runs before orchestrator waves when enabled.
- charts/redwood-private-installer/NOTES.txt: Updated to explain airgap flow and fail-open vs. fail-closed behavior.
- charts/redwood-private-installer/README.md and docs/private-installer.md: Documentation for configuring orchestrator DSL, timeouts, and recommended mirror layouts.
- tests/values-airgap.yaml and tests/template-tests/init-orchestrator-test.yaml: Examples and assertions covering the main branching behaviors.

Commits (summary):
- 1f3a2d2 Add initial orchestrator DSL templates and helpers
- b4c8d9f Add preflight image verification job and schema validations
- 9e7f4a1 Wire up values and add example airgap values file
- 3c2b8f7 Add unit template tests and CI pipeline step for airgap tests
- 5a1b0e3 Fix: parameterize backoff policy and expose leader-election annotation

Design notes and rationale:
- Orchestrator DSL is intentionally minimal (waves->stages->tasks) so the template stays readable and control plane logic remains in a tiny, audited init-controller container instead of complex Helm hooks. This reduces Helm lifecycle surprises while enabling deterministic ordering across tenants.
- The preflight image verification supports two modes: manifest (ConfigMap with image:digest entries) and mirror-check (attempts registry pull using provided credentials). In air-gapped installs, operators can supply a manifest, and the Job will gate the install if essential images are missing unless allowMissingImages=true is set.
- Concurrency: .Values.initOrchestrator.maxConcurrentWaves can be scoped per-tenant (we emit tenant labels) so platform operators can limit parallel seed jobs.

Review conversation (high level, single continuous narrative):
- Evelyn Park: "Can we make the backoff policy configurable per-wave rather than global? Some tenants have slow seed tasks."
- Author (Anya): "Good point — initial patch had a global setting. Updated to allow per-wave backoff and a sane global default; added schema and tests."
- Marcus Li: "Security: the preflight job touches registry credentials. Please ensure we don't log secrets and add a note about using projected service account tokens or KMS for credentials."
- Author: "Agreed. The Job uses a Kubernetes Secret volume mounted as a file; I added log redaction in the init-controller and documentation recommending projected service account tokens for short-lived credentials. Also added an RBAC snippet restricting the init-controller to Job/ConfigMap access only."
- Ravi Sharma: "Nit: helper names collide with existing prefix. Rename orchestration helpers to 'rpOrch' to avoid collisions."
- Author: "Renamed helper functions and updated templates accordingly."
- Evelyn Park (approval): "Approach looks good, tests exercise the main paths. Approving pending CI green."

CI and verification:
- Pipeline: linters -> helm unit tests -> template-tests (airgap) -> integration smoke on k3s runner. First run had one flake in integration (timeout on k3s job startup). Re-ran the integration stage; all checks passed. Final status: pass.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- This change is additive. initOrchestrator is disabled by default. Existing installs are unaffected unless operators opt-in. Schema additions are backward compatible with previous values files.

Manual test scenarios performed by author:
- Airgapped install using tests/values-airgap.yaml with manifest mode and mirror mode against local registry mirror.
- Non-airgap install with orchestrator enabled and multiple tenant labels to validate per-tenant concurrency gating.
- Simulated missing image in manifest to verify fail-open vs fail-closed behavior.

Follow-ups & TODOs (tracked in Linear):
- ENG-1987: add an optional controller mode to run the orchestrator as a Deployment instead of a Job for very large clusters (future work).
- ENG-2032: extend preflight checks to validate OCI signatures and attestations.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after CLA and DCO checks. Changelog entry included in release notes.

Files changed (illustrative snippets):
- templates/init-orchestrator-job.yaml (new): renders when .Values.initOrchestrator.enabled == true and consumes .Values.initOrchestrator.dsl. Job is annotated with "rp.redwood.com/init-wave": "{{ .wave }}" to help tracing.
- templates/preflight-image-check.yaml (new): conditional on .Values.airgapVerification.enabled; mounts secret 'airgap-registry-credentials' when provided.
- values.schema.json (modified): new definitions for initOrchestrator and airgapVerification with enum validations and regex for image digests.

If you want to test locally: helm template ./charts/redwood-private-installer -f tests/values-airgap.yaml --set initOrchestrator.enabled=true | less

Notes: This PR purposefully keeps the orchestrator controller image minimal. The controller intentionally performs no destructive actions other than creating Jobs; all real changes are surfaced as Jobs/ConfigMaps so operators can audit them easily. The preflight job does not retry image pulls by default in manifest mode (it verifies digests), but mirror-check can be configured for retries.
